answer: Join-fee burn blocks bulk fake identities. A new identity burns a 40-credit fee and gets a jade stamp receipt on a public mirror ledger. In a burst the fee rises: the k-th join costs 40+6(k-1) credits on a ferrous schedule. Forging 1,000 identities in one burst burns 3,037,000 credits against a 40,000 pool, so the attack loses money. Spacing joins to dodge the surge fails: the fee averages three epochs. An honest agent pays 40 credits once.
